title: Machine learning guided discovery of enhanced anomalous Hall resistivity in Fe–Ir–Pt films
summary: A machine-learning screen trained on experimental Fe–heavy-element binary alloys pointed to a ternary Fe–Ir–Pt composition range with enhanced anomalous Hall effect. High-throughput composition-spread measurements experimentally found a peak anomalous Hall resistivity of 6.5 μΩ·cm, above the prior 5.25 μΩ·cm maximum reported for Fe–X binary systems. Scaling analysis attributed the enhancement to an extrinsic contribution.
ai_technology: Gaussian process regression using Magpie composition descriptors

evidence.tested: A machine-learning screen trained on experimental Fe–heavy-element binary alloys pointed to a ternary Fe–Ir–Pt composition range with enhanced anomalous Hall effect.
evidence.unknown: This is a thin-film anomalous Hall resistivity result; the paper does not demonstrate a finished magnetic sensor or device. The machine-learning model overpredicted absolute values for the measured Fe–Ir–Pt compositions, although it qualitatively identified the enhancement and composition trend. The reported extrinsic origin comes from the paper’s scaling analysis. The result is limited to the measured composition-spread films and does not establish performance across bulk material forms or devices.
evidence.ai_role: The model was trained on measured Fe–X binary anomalous Hall data and screened 13,260 possible Fe-based ternary compositions for a larger effect. Its predicted Fe–Ir–Pt region guided experimental testing in composition-spread films; the machine-learning prediction and high-throughput measurement together identified the enhanced-effect composition range.
